title: Authentication
body:
Authentication answers **who are you?** — it's the act of proving identity, by presenting something the server can verify: a password, a session cookie, an API key, an OAuth token, a JWT. In the restaurant analogy it's showing your membership card before ordering.

Credentials are presented by the client and checked by the server; the check must always happen on the server, since anything on the [[Frontend]] can be read and modified by the user. A failed authentication is what produces **401 Unauthorized** — despite the name, 401 is about identity, not permission. Don't conflate this with [[Authorization]], which is the separate question of what a verified identity is allowed to do.
